description: We are Astronomical Observers team aiming for challenge 12 planet X and SPHEREx. Looking for web developers and UI UX designers to join us. so who is ready?
summary:
Our universe is full of secrets, so why can't we show it to people and teach them more about it? Yes, that is our mission today by using NASA's telescope SPHEREx and its data. But the problem is not the telescope, it's the data inside it. Most of the students see this data and start to think it's very hard to understand those complex ideas, and that is why we started our project 'SPHEREx Base Station' as a starting point for every student and explorer, a beacon of hope for the new generation of students, So here our mission starts to help them discover the universe.

Our platform is designed specifically for students and space lovers. We took this challenge to share knowledge in a fun and simple way, because we noticed that science can sometimes feel dry and boring, and there haven't been enough interactive spaces to turn complex ideas into captivating stories that capture students' hearts. We built our web on one simple idea: instead of showing students confusing tables, we created an interactive sky map that makes space data easy to see. We also added a smart AI guide that helps students to read data, plus we have created interactive games—such as investigations and laboratory-based activities—to develop students' skills , all in an engaging way that stimulates and nourishes their minds.

By using the great power of the internet for learning, we are making scientists, detectives, readers, and finally humans that love science and adore it .
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

  • Using data from NASA's SPHEREx telescope, the platform ("SPHEREx Base Station") replaces confusing tables with an easy flash cards that makes space data easy to see. It also includes books and labs to help students read the data, as well as interactive research hub to help student's improve their research skills.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Shares knowledge in a fun and simple way.
  • Develops students' skills in inquiry, analysis, and problem-solving.
  • Stimulates and nourishes students' minds in an engaging way.
  • Helps students choose their passion and discover the universe.
  • Turns complex ideas into captivating stories that capture students' heart

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • To act as a starting point for every student and explorer, and a beacon of hope for the new generation of students.
  • To create scientists, detectives, readers, and humans who love and adore science.
  • To raise a new, hopeful generation that can think deeply and solve hard problems.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • We used Python programming language along with the Base 44 development platform to build our web platform. Additionally, the project utilizes data from NASA's SPHEREx telescope, integrating AI for the smart guide, an interactive sky map, and lab-based games.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Instead of showing confusing tables or presenting dry science, the project builds on a simple, engaging idea: turning space data into an interactive sky map, adding a smart AI guide to assist with reading data, and creating interactive games (investigations and lab-based activities) to turn complex ideas into captivating stories, and a digital awards and academic titles to motivate students.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Most students see telescope data as very hard to understand due to its complex ideas.
  • Science can sometimes feel dry and boring.
  • There haven't been enough interactive spaces to turn complex ideas into captivating stories that capture students' hearts.
